Seminar Title:

Development and Characterization of Gellan Gum- Based Emulgels for Functional Bakery Application

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Saswatee Subhadarshinee Ojha

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall (BM-140)

Date and Time:

10 Nov 2026 10:45 AM

Contact:

Dr. Prasoon Kumar

Abstract:

Conventional emulsions are physically unstable; immobilizing lipid droplets in a three-dimensional network gives stable emulgels, but the structural effect of progressively raising lipid content in a fixed polysaccharide network is poorly understood. Here, 2% w/w gellan gum (GLG) emulgels with 0–25% w/w rice bran oil (RBO) were studied by inversion testing, brightfield and confocal microscopy, impedance analysis, colorimetry, visible reflectance spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging. All formulations were self-supporting; RBO droplets increased in number and size yet stayed discrete within the GLG network up to 25% RBO. Impedance was linked to obstruction of the aqueous conduction pathway by oil droplets. More RBO increased yellowness and decreased whiteness, and hyperspectral imaging corroborated the microscopic and colorimetric trends. Uniquely, this work connects microstructure, electrical behaviour, optical properties and spatial hyperspectral data, supporting GLG–RBO emulgels as structurally stable lipid-structuring systems for functional bakery applications, including steamed bread.
